A developer builds a SQL query with string interpolation, and the app crashes on certain inputs:

final name = request.url.queryParameters['name'] ?? '';
final results = await conn.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '$name'");
parameter is interpolated directly into the SQL string. If a user passes
SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ''; DROP TABLE users; --'
— a catastrophic SQL injection. Even without a DROP, an attacker could read arbitrary data.
placeholder is substituted safely by the driver (escaping/parameter separation). The
value is never parsed as SQL — it's a data parameter.
: never interpolate user input into SQL strings. Always use parameterized queries (
/args). SQL injection is a top security vulnerability. The parameterized query is the only safe way.
